mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-theory-01.stem: A chemical label depicting a fish and tree concerns harm to the aquatic environment; also check the label and SDS for the substance name and safe concentration.
reasons: True. The picture provides a clue to harm to aquatic organisms or the environment. Check the label and SDS for the substance’s identity and detailed control measures.
Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Interpreting the fish picture as indicating drinking or washing use is wrong; treat it as notification of environmental hazards.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-theory-02.stem: The harder you strike the head of a bolt that is difficult to insert, the more its thread compatibility is guaranteed.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Striking may crush the threads. Check the part number, alignment, foreign matter and damage as possible causes of difficult insertion; do not force the bolt tight.
False. Striking may crush the threads. Check the part number, alignment, foreign matter and damage as possible causes of difficult insertion; do not force the bolt tight.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-theory-03.stem: High electrical conductivity alone does not establish suitability as a component; the required cross section, temperature, connections and specifications must also be checked.
reasons: True. Metals such as copper and aluminum conduct readily and are used in wiring. Good conductivity alone does not establish component suitability: check the required cross-section, temperature, connections and specifications. Do not substitute a similarly colored material without authorization.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Metals such as copper and aluminum conduct readily and are used in wiring. Good conductivity alone does not establish component suitability: check the required cross-section, temperature, connections and specifications. Do not substitute a similarly colored material without authorization.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-theory-04.stem: Preventive maintenance means checking conditions to prevent failures and accidents, rather than only repairing equipment after it breaks down.
reasons: True. Preventive maintenance is an approach to checking equipment condition to prevent failures and accidents, rather than only repairing it after a breakdown. Daily checks cover specified items before work and at other designated times to detect small changes early. Periodic inspections follow a plan and examine details that daily checks alone may not reveal. Performing one does not permit omission of the other.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Preventive maintenance is an approach to checking equipment condition to prevent failures and accidents, rather than only repairing it after a breakdown. Daily checks cover specified items before work and at other designated times to detect small changes early. Periodic inspections follow a plan and examine details that daily checks alone may not reveal. Performing one does not permit omission of the other.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-theory-05.stem: Passing a mock exam makes all required workplace training and work permits unnecessary.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. A mock exam checks learning and does not grant qualifications, training or work permits for actual equipment. Confirm the necessary requirements and assigned responsibilities at the workplace.
False. A mock exam checks learning and does not grant qualifications, training or work permits for actual equipment. Confirm the necessary requirements and assigned responsibilities at the workplace.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-theory-06.stem: If visual inspection finds no cracks, it can also guarantee the absence of internal defects.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. The surface visible in visual inspection differs from the interior. Internal defects require an inspection method appropriate to the material, location and requirements.
False. The surface visible in visual inspection differs from the interior. Internal defects require an inspection method appropriate to the material, location and requirements.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-theory-07.stem: Geometrical tolerances specify straightness, flatness, roundness, parallelism, perpendicularity, position and other characteristics.
reasons: True. Even if a diameter or length is within its specified range, requirements for surface flatness, axis orientation or position may not be met. Geometrical tolerances indicate characteristics such as straightness, flatness, roundness, parallelism, perpendicularity and position. Different types evaluate different properties, so one dimensional measurement does not mean everything has been checked.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Even if a diameter or length is within its specified range, requirements for surface flatness, axis orientation or position may not be met. Geometrical tolerances indicate characteristics such as straightness, flatness, roundness, parallelism, perpendicularity and position. Different types evaluate different properties, so one dimensional measurement does not mean everything has been checked.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-theory-08.stem: Calculating the thickness reduction percentage automatically determines the permissible amount of processing in one pass on the actual workpiece.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. The reduction percentage is a geometric ratio relative to the original thickness. The permissible amount of processing in one pass depends on the material, equipment capability and approved process.

False. The reduction percentage is a geometric ratio relative to the original thickness. The permissible amount of processing in one pass depends on the material, equipment capability and approved process.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-theory-09.stem: If a marking is readable, checking whether its content matches the product is unnecessary.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Even a readable marking may show a different part number or incorrect quantity. Separately check that the marking matches the actual product.
False. Even a readable marking may show a different part number or incorrect quantity. Separately check that the marking matches the actual product.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-theory-10.stem: Dimensions provide information needed for a component’s function and manufacture and generally indicate finished dimensions.
reasons: True. Dimensions give the information needed for a part’s function and manufacture and normally specify its finished dimensions. Repeating the same dimension unnecessarily can cause conflicting values after a change. Even if the drawing is printed large, read its stated dimensions rather than measuring the paper with a ruler as a substitute for the requirement.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Dimensions give the information needed for a part’s function and manufacture and normally specify its finished dimensions. Repeating the same dimension unnecessarily can cause conflicting values after a change. Even if the drawing is printed large, read its stated dimensions rather than measuring the paper with a ruler as a substitute for the requirement.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-theory-11.stem: Ra and Rz can be standardized to the largest value, disregarding which surface each requirement concerns.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Ra and Rz are roughness parameters with different definitions. Retain the parameter and value specified for each surface; do not standardize them to the maximum value.
False. Ra and Rz are roughness parameters with different definitions. Retain the parameter and value specified for each surface; do not standardize them to the maximum value.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-theory-12.stem: Use the type of protective equipment specified for your work and check for damage, dirt and proper fit before use.
reasons:
True. Protective equipment is used to shield the body from danger. Safety footwear, protective glasses, and gloves may differ in performance and purpose even when they share the same name. Use the type specified for your task and inspect it for damage, dirt, and proper fit before use.
Gloves protect hands during activities such as handling sharp material. However, they can become a source of danger in work where a rotating tool could catch them. Do not wear gloves while drilling with a drill press. Keep hands away from rotating parts and observe the prohibitions in the procedure.
Wearing protective glasses does not permit removal of a machine guard. Protective equipment must be used together with equipment safety measures and correct working methods. Check that its performance is appropriate for hazards such as flying particles, chemicals, or dust.
If the equipment does not fit, obscures your view, or is damaged, do not tolerate the problem and continue working; ask for replacement or adjustment. Do not substitute another person’s protective equipment without permission.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Protective equipment is used to shield the body from danger. Safety footwear, protective glasses, and gloves may differ in performance and purpose even when they share the same name. Use the type specified for your task and inspect it for damage, dirt, and proper fit before use.
Gloves protect hands during activities such as handling sharp material. However, they can become a source of danger in work where a rotating tool could catch them. Do not wear gloves while drilling with a drill press. Keep hands away from rotating parts and observe the prohibitions in the procedure.
Wearing protective glasses does not permit removal of a machine guard. Protective equipment must be used together with equipment safety measures and correct working methods. Check that its performance is appropriate for hazards such as flying particles, chemicals, or dust.
If the equipment does not fit, obscures your view, or is damaged, do not tolerate the problem and continue working; ask for replacement or adjustment. Do not substitute another person’s protective equipment without permission.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-theory-13.stem: Before work, confirm the equipment assigned to you, work procedure, stopping method and contact person.
reasons:
True. Familiarity alone cannot determine whether a machine is safe. Before work, confirm the equipment you are responsible for, the procedure, how to stop it, and whom to contact. Do not operate an unfamiliar machine or one whose controls you do not understand on your own initiative.
If you notice an unusual sound, smell, or vibration during work, give priority to preventing danger from spreading rather than finding a reason to continue. Stop the machine using the prescribed procedure and notify the person responsible from a safe position. Never put your hand into a running machine to remove chips or parts.
When reporting, state the equipment name, when you noticed the condition, the facts observed, and the action already taken. Saying only “I think it is broken” makes it difficult for the listener to assess the situation. Separate assumptions from facts if the cause is not yet confirmed. Even after stopping, do not restart the machine or open a cover to investigate without permission.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Familiarity alone cannot determine whether a machine is safe. Before work, confirm the equipment you are responsible for, the procedure, how to stop it, and whom to contact. Do not operate an unfamiliar machine or one whose controls you do not understand on your own initiative.
If you notice an unusual sound, smell, or vibration during work, give priority to preventing danger from spreading rather than finding a reason to continue. Stop the machine using the prescribed procedure and notify the person responsible from a safe position. Never put your hand into a running machine to remove chips or parts.
When reporting, state the equipment name, when you noticed the condition, the facts observed, and the action already taken. Saying only “I think it is broken” makes it difficult for the listener to assess the situation. Separate assumptions from facts if the cause is not yet confirmed. Even after stopping, do not restart the machine or open a cover to investigate without permission.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-theory-14.stem: If a container is the same color as the adjacent liquid, its contents can be identified definitively even if its label is unknown.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Color does not establish a substance’s identity. Do not use a liquid whose identification is unclear; ask the responsible person to check the container and original records.
False. Color does not establish a substance’s identity. Do not use a liquid whose identification is unclear; ask the responsible person to check the container and original records.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-theory-15.stem: First check the front view and projection-method instructions to avoid confusing left and right on the paper with the direction from which the actual object is viewed.
reasons: True. A projection view represents the shape of a solid object on a plane. In third-angle projection, the top view, seen from above, is placed above the front view, and the right-side view, seen from the right, is placed to its right. First check the front view and the stated projection method so you do not confuse left and right on the paper with the direction from which the object is viewed.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. A projection view represents the shape of a solid object on a plane. In third-angle projection, the top view, seen from above, is placed above the front view, and the right-side view, seen from the right, is placed to its right. First check the front view and the stated projection method so you do not confuse left and right on the paper with the direction from which the object is viewed.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-theory-16.stem: The nonconforming-unit rate of an inspected sample guarantees conformity of every uninspected item.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. The sample rate is a result for the inspected items, not a result from checking every uninspected item. Lot acceptance also requires the specified sampling criteria.
False. The sample rate is a result for the inspected items, not a result from checking every uninspected item. Lot acceptance also requires the specified sampling criteria.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-theory-17.stem: A QC process chart organizes what is controlled at each process, by what method, at what frequency, and what action is taken when an abnormality occurs.
reasons: True. A work standard specifies the work content, sequence, equipment, tools, and important conditions to maintain required quality despite changes in people or time. A QC process chart organizes what is controlled in each process, how often and by what method, and how abnormalities are handled. The working method and the control system play different roles even in the same process.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. A work standard specifies the work content, sequence, equipment, tools, and important conditions to maintain required quality despite changes in people or time. A QC process chart organizes what is controlled in each process, how often and by what method, and how abnormalities are handled. The working method and the control system play different roles even in the same process.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-theory-18.stem: If the items are the correct type, the three fixed principles are maintained even when the shelf’s quantity limit is exceeded.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. The three fixed principles include quantity as well as location and item type. Exceeding the quantity limit violates the fixed-quantity principle even for the correct items.
False. The three fixed principles include quantity as well as location and item type. Exceeding the quantity limit violates the fixed-quantity principle even for the correct items.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-theory-19.stem: A dial indicator comparison reading of 0.03 mm always indicates the workpiece’s full dimension.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. A comparison reading is the difference from a reference. Obtain the full dimension by adding the signed difference to the reference dimension.
False. A comparison reading is the difference from a reference. Obtain the full dimension by adding the signed difference to the reference dimension.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-theory-20.stem: Use the workplace’s prescribed assessment method to prioritize risks; do not decide solely by personal impressions.
reasons:
True. When considering risk, look not only at whether a hazard exists but also at the severity of an accident, its likelihood, and opportunities for exposure. Use the workplace’s assessment method rather than deciding priorities solely by personal intuition.
First consider whether the hazard can be eliminated or reduced. If equipment or process changes are needed, consult the responsible person or department instead of modifying equipment without authorization. After implementation, check whether the measure works and whether a new hazard has been created.
Maintaining safety requires repeating a cycle of planning, implementation, evaluation, and necessary improvement. Inspection records and near misses provide information for the next improvement.
Do not assume that countermeasures completely eliminate the possibility of an accident. Machines can fail, misunderstandings can occur, and surroundings can change. Share the remaining hazards and maintain the ability to stop when something abnormal occurs.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. When considering risk, look not only at whether a hazard exists but also at the severity of an accident, its likelihood, and opportunities for exposure. Use the workplace’s assessment method rather than deciding priorities solely by personal intuition.
First consider whether the hazard can be eliminated or reduced. If equipment or process changes are needed, consult the responsible person or department instead of modifying equipment without authorization. After implementation, check whether the measure works and whether a new hazard has been created.
Maintaining safety requires repeating a cycle of planning, implementation, evaluation, and necessary improvement. Inspection records and near misses provide information for the next improvement.
Do not assume that countermeasures completely eliminate the possibility of an accident. Machines can fail, misunderstandings can occur, and surroundings can change. Share the remaining hazards and maintain the ability to stop when something abnormal occurs.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-theory-21.stem: A smaller roughness value is not unconditionally better for every function.
reasons: True. Surface roughness describes small surface irregularities and relates to friction, wear, lubrication, and appearance. Ra is arithmetic mean roughness and Rz is maximum-height roughness. Check the parameter, unit, and measurement conditions against the drawing requirement. A smaller roughness value is not unconditionally better for every function.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Surface roughness describes small surface irregularities and relates to friction, wear, lubrication, and appearance. Ra is arithmetic mean roughness and Rz is maximum-height roughness. Check the parameter, unit, and measurement conditions against the drawing requirement. A smaller roughness value is not unconditionally better for every function.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-theory-22.stem: If polishing makes a surface shiny, an out-of-specification outside diameter also becomes acceptable.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Gloss does not guarantee conformity of the outside diameter. Check dimensions and surface condition as separate requirements.
False. Gloss does not guarantee conformity of the outside diameter. Check dimensions and surface condition as separate requirements.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-theory-23.stem: If one person knows about the new revision, informing the next person in charge is unnecessary.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Unless the next person in charge is also informed of when the new revision takes effect, its scope and how it is distinguished from the old revision, work may be performed under different conditions.

False. Unless the next person in charge is also informed of when the new revision takes effect, its scope and how it is distinguished from the old revision, work may be performed under different conditions.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-theory-24.stem: Safety signs include those prohibiting actions, warning of hazards, and identifying places or equipment needed in an emergency.
reasons:
True. Safety signs include those that prohibit actions, warn of a hazard, and indicate locations or equipment needed in an emergency. Do not only memorize the picture; consider what action is required at that location.
“No entry” does not mean you may enter if you are careful. An electric-shock warning indicates the presence of an electrical hazard. Follow the sign and confirm the equipment procedure and your authorization to enter the area.
For chemicals, check the container label and safety data sheet. Hazards such as ignition, corrosion, and health effects differ by substance. Do not identify contents solely by color or smell, or use liquid from an unlabeled container.
Check the locations and routes to fire extinguishers, AEDs, and evacuation areas during normal conditions instead of starting to search in an emergency. If an escape route is obstructed, request improvement according to workplace rules.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Safety signs include those that prohibit actions, warn of a hazard, and indicate locations or equipment needed in an emergency. Do not only memorize the picture; consider what action is required at that location.
“No entry” does not mean you may enter if you are careful. An electric-shock warning indicates the presence of an electrical hazard. Follow the sign and confirm the equipment procedure and your authorization to enter the area.
For chemicals, check the container label and safety data sheet. Hazards such as ignition, corrosion, and health effects differ by substance. Do not identify contents solely by color or smell, or use liquid from an unlabeled container.
Check the locations and routes to fire extinguishers, AEDs, and evacuation areas during normal conditions instead of starting to search in an emergency. If an escape route is obstructed, request improvement according to workplace rules.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-theory-25.stem: After periodic inspection is completed, the next day’s daily inspection is unnecessary.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Daily and periodic inspections differ in scope and purpose. Yesterday’s periodic inspection does not replace this morning’s check for leaks and other conditions.
False. Daily and periodic inspections differ in scope and purpose. Yesterday’s periodic inspection does not replace this morning’s check for leaks and other conditions.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-theory-26.stem: If a hole diameter becomes out of specification after the tool and operator are changed simultaneously, investigate both changes and other 4M conditions rather than declaring only one the cause.
reasons: True. When the operator and tool change simultaneously, the sequence of events alone cannot identify one as the cause. Check the facts for the 4Ms, including mounting, materials, settings and methods.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. When the operator and tool change simultaneously, the sequence of events alone cannot identify one as the cause. Check the facts for the 4Ms, including mounting, materials, settings and methods.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-theory-27.stem: Knowing the numerical setting makes checking its unit unnecessary.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. The same numerical value represents a different quantity when the unit differs. Check a setting’s number together with its displayed unit.
False. The same numerical value represents a different quantity when the unit differs. Check a setting’s number together with its displayed unit.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-theory-28.stem: For slinging and operation, verify required qualifications, training and assigned responsibilities; someone merely nearby must not start assisting on their own initiative.
reasons: True. A crane load can fall because of a wire-rope or attachment problem. Stay out from under the load and outside designated danger areas; follow access control and signals. Slinging and operation require the necessary qualifications, training and assigned scope. A nearby bystander must not independently start helping.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. A crane load can fall because of a wire-rope or attachment problem. Stay out from under the load and outside designated danger areas; follow access control and signals. Slinging and operation require the necessary qualifications, training and assigned scope. A nearby bystander must not independently start helping.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-theory-29.stem: Read prohibition and warning signs separately: prohibition signs identify actions that must not be performed, while warning signs identify existing hazards.
reasons: True. Prohibition communicates a restriction on behavior, while a warning communicates the presence of a hazard. It does not mean that acting carefully removes a prohibition.
Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Treating a warning sign as permission to act confuses the roles of prohibitions and hazard notifications.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-theory-30.stem: For every threaded NO-GO gauge, judgment is based solely on the same insertion behavior as a plain hole.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Threaded NO-GO gauges are judged under specified conditions such as insertion behavior and number of turns. Do not unconditionally apply the passage criteria for a plain hole.
False. Threaded NO-GO gauges are judged under specified conditions such as insertion behavior and number of turns. Do not unconditionally apply the passage criteria for a plain hole.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-practical-01.stem: The cutting sound changes suddenly, but no scratches are yet visible on the product. Which action is appropriate, including the decision to restart?
options: Stop safely and report; obtain separate instructions for checking the product and restarting the equipment.
Restart immediately on your own judgment after stopping.
Record the cause definitively as a breakdown.
reasons: Continuing until scratches appear can allow an equipment abnormality to increase hazards and defects.
Stop safely, report the facts, and separately check the product impact and whether equipment restart is permitted.
Do not restart without authorization until the cause and safety have been checked, even after stopping.
A breakdown is a suspected cause; record it separately from the observed fact of an abnormal sound.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-practical-02.stem: The new work standard is available, but it is unclear whether the QC process chart is an old revision. How should you proceed?
options: Follow only the work standard and omit measurement.
Set control values from old memories.
Check the scope and revision of both documents and the applicability of their control conditions.
Treat the fixing method as unnecessary because measurement was performed.
reasons: Following the work method does not allow omission of measurements specified in the QC process chart.
Old memories do not verify the control conditions for the current product and revision.
The work standard and QC process chart have different roles; cross-check the scope, revision and applicable conditions of both.
A measurement result does not eliminate the work-method requirement to secure the material.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-practical-03.stem: The basic size is 12 mm, the upper deviation is +0.03 mm, and the lower deviation is −0.01 mm. What is the tolerance?
reasons: Subtracting the lower limit, 11.99 mm, from the upper limit, 12.03 mm, gives 0.04 mm.
This treats the positive and negative deviations like a sum rather than a difference and differs from the tolerance of 0.04 mm.
Tolerance is the difference between the limit sizes, not a value obtained by adding the basic size of 12 mm.
Adding the upper and lower limits gives 24.02 mm, which is not the tolerance.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-practical-04.stem: There is an uncoated area on the back of an outdoor component. Its front is uniform. How should you judge it?
options: If only the front looks clean, all requirements pass.
Check the surfaces requiring corrosion protection, coating condition and required inspections against the requirements.
Use any paint if its color is the same.
reasons: The attractive front cannot compensate for missing coating on a back surface that requires corrosion protection.
Compare the target surfaces, coating condition, thickness and other items with requirements; confirm required inspections and approved disposition.
Unapproved recoating may violate specified film thickness or curing conditions.
Paints of the same color may differ in composition and performance, so compatibility with the specified paint must be checked.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-practical-05.stem: The inside diameter at the entrance was measured, but the contact tip cannot reach a groove farther inside. How should this be recorded?
options: Copy the entrance diameter as the groove diameter.
Record measurement as complete because the pointer moved.
Force the contact tip to bend.
Record the groove as unverified and consult about a suitable contact shape and reference.
reasons: The entrance and groove are different locations; do not copy the entrance diameter as the groove diameter.
Pointer movement alone does not establish contact with the groove’s measuring surface.
Bending the contact tip damages its geometry, function or measurement conditions; do not modify it without authorization.
Record the unreachable groove as unverified and consult about a tip shape that can make contact, its range and the reference.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-practical-06.stem: The angle of an inclined surface was readable, but the protractor’s base was not contacting the intended surface. What should you do?
options: Use only the number that was readable.
Correct contact with both surfaces and verify using the specified method.
Convert it to a length as a substitute.
Replace it with the angle of an easier-to-view surface.
reasons: A reading taken without base contact does not guarantee the angle between the two specified surfaces.
Place the base and blade correctly against the two intended surfaces and verify the angle using the specified method.
Angle and length are different quantities; conversion does not correct poor contact.
The angle of another surface does not replace the requested target angle.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-practical-07.stem: Incorrect labels on purchased items are repeatedly found during inspection. Which approach should a small group use?
options: Declare inspection alone to be the cause.
Determine the cause by majority vote alone.
Collect facts from procurement through shipment and check the effectiveness of countermeasures.
reasons: Even when inspection discovers the issue, investigate possible causes in procurement, labeling, handover and other stages.
A majority vote selects an opinion; it does not prove a cause as fact.
Investigate facts and handovers from procurement through shipment, and check whether identification is maintained after countermeasures.
Changing labeling conditions also requires formal checking and approval.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-practical-08.stem: Defects are classified as A: 8 cases, B: 7 cases, and C: 5 cases. What percentage is A alone?
reasons: 8 is a count; obtain its percentage of all 20 cases using 8 ÷ 20 × 100.
75% represents the combined 15 cases of A and B, not A alone.
The 8 cases of A represent 40%; 60% represents the remaining 12 cases.
A accounts for 8 of the total 20 cases, so 8 ÷ 20 × 100 = 40%.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-practical-09.stem: Thickness decreases from 4.0 mm to 3.0 mm. What is the reduction percentage relative to the original thickness?
reasons: Dividing the reduction of 1.0 mm by the original thickness of 4.0 mm gives 25%.
33.3% uses the final thickness of 3.0 mm as the denominator, rather than the original thickness.
75% represents the remaining 3.0 mm, not the reduction percentage.
A reduction of 1 mm cannot simply be treated as 1%.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-practical-10.stem: You are selecting a fiber-reinforced resin component. How should you assess the material?
options: Check the combination of resin and reinforcement and the specified conditions.
Remove all fibers as foreign matter.
The resin name alone guarantees all performance.
reasons: Properties are obtained through the combination of resin and reinforcement such as fibers; check the composition and specified conditions.
Fibers added for reinforcement are not foreign matter; removing them without authorization changes the material’s composition.
Reinforcements also include glass fibers and other materials; they are not limited to metals.
Even with the same resin name, performance differs with reinforcement, molding conditions and other factors, so the name does not guarantee all requirements.
